subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should builtin `memorySearch.extraPaths` accept arbitrary JSONL logs, or should raw hook logs stay in QMD, session-memory, converter, or plugin workflows?
rationale: The code shape is clear, but adding arbitrary JSONL ingestion expands the builtin memory boundary and changes sensitive-data handling and provider-upload semantics.

options.title: Require a safe ingestion contract
options.body: Keep this open but do not queue implementation until maintainers choose allowed JSONL shapes, field selection/redaction, line mapping, and provider-upload behavior.

options.title: Document an external workflow
options.body: If arbitrary raw JSONL is out of builtin scope, document the supported QMD, session-memory, converter, or plugin workflow and close against that product decision.

options.title: Implement native support
options.body: After product and security review, update discovery, parsing/chunking, watcher behavior, `memory_get`, docs, and focused tests together.

recommendation.title: Require a safe ingestion contract
recommendation.body: Keep this open but do not queue implementation until maintainers choose allowed JSONL shapes, field selection/redaction, line mapping, and provider-upload behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-host refactor history and live issue routing make steipete the best available owner for deciding whether this belongs in builtin memory or an external/plugin workflow.
